LMP3.title: United’s stand-in pairing wins a rain-stopped LMP3 class
LMP3.dek: Falb and last-minute substitute Andrews won for United’s #2 Ligier after rain halted the race, from eighth on the class grid, with RLR MSport second and 360 Racing third.

facts.v: Andrews, called up when Rayhall fell ill, scored his first ELMS victory alongside Falb, whose previous class win had come more than a year earlier.

chapters.title: A title race still wide open
text: LMP3 reached Spa with the table tight. RLR MSport’s Ligier #15 of Farano, van Uitert and Garofall led on 58.5 points after wins at Le Castellet and the Red Bull Ring, twelve clear of United’s #3 and Eurointernational’s #11. 360 Racing’s #6 sat half a point further back and Inter Europol’s #13 a point behind that. A sixth place at Silverstone had cost RLR some ground, but its margin was enough to make a first title clinch possible in Belgium, if rivals suffered a very bad weekend.

Eighteen cars were entered. DKR Engineering’s Norma was back after skipping Silverstone, taking the slot left by the one-off Virage Ligier. United had to change a line-up at short notice: Rayhall was too ill to travel, so Le Mans Cup regular Scott Andrews stepped into the #2 beside Falb. On Saturday morning van Uitert topped LMP3 practice for RLR, less than a tenth up on the Ultimate Norma, with Eurointernational’s #11 six tenths back. A poor forecast then led organisers to move Sunday’s start from 12:30 to 10:45.

chapters.title: Lahaye takes a third pole
text: Matthieu Lahaye put the Ultimate Norma #17 on pole with a 2:13.634, the team’s third of the season, on a track that was close to dry. Drudi was just 0.065s adrift in Eurointernational’s #11, and Kaiser slotted the 360 Racing Ligier #6 into third by getting ahead of Noble’s Ecurie Ecosse/Nielsen car #7 at the very end. Van Uitert was fifth in the points-leading RLR car.

The pace was extremely close, with the top ten inside a second. Andrews qualified the United #2 eighth in class on his ELMS debut, with Bell in sister car #3 tenth. Eurointernational’s second Ligier, #12, was last of the 18 on a 2:24.588.

chapters.title: Safety car and early casualties
text: LMP3 lost cars early. Trouble for the pole-sitting Ultimate Norma and for AT Racing’s Ligier #9 brought out a safety car for about 20 minutes, with the field running behind it a couple of laps longer than planned. Neither car was classified at the end, and BHK Motorsport’s Ligier #16 was another entry that never reached the chequered flag as an official finisher.

chapters.title: Rain takes over
text: When green came back RLR’s van Uitert and Drudi disputed the lead, and as the rain grew heavier the Ligiers were repeatedly caught out and the safety car was needed more than once. Cool Racing’s Borga set the class fastest lap, a 2:38.152, in the worsening conditions. By the time the race was stopped United’s #2 had worked its way to the front under Falb, with RLR’s #15 second and 360 Racing’s #6 third. Eurointernational’s #12, among the cars in trouble, finished on 31 laps.

chapters.title: Called with the cars on the pit straight
text: Race Control stopped the race with close to two hours of the four still to run, and the cars were lined up on the pit straight while officials considered a restart. Officials later called it off for good. Because the two-hour mark had been passed, the result stood and half points were awarded. That made Falb and Andrews winners in the United #2, a class win that came from eighth on the class grid.

chapters.title: United wins both prototype classes
text: The #2 won on 40 laps, with RLR’s #15 second, 360 Racing’s #6 third and United’s #3 fourth, both a lap down. M. Racing - YMR’s Ligier #18 was fifth and Cool Racing’s #4 sixth, ahead of Oregon Team’s Norma #10. Ultimate’s #17, AT Racing’s #9 and BHK’s #16 were not classified. United took the LMP3 win to go with its LMP2 victory, and the standings stayed open for the Portimão finale on 28 October, with RLR still at the head of the table.

chapters.title: Proton leads, JMW and Spirit of Race chase
text: Six LMGTE cars lined up at Spa. Gianluca and Giorgio Roda’s Proton Porsche #88 led the table by nine points, thanks to a win and two second places from the first four races, and Cairoli was back alongside them for a fourth time this season. JMW Motorsport’s Ferrari #66 of MacDowall, Griffin and Molina was second and had again been drawn into a late-season title fight. Spirit of Race’s #55 was third, only five points back, and still in contention for the second automatic Le Mans entry.

Practice favoured Porsche. Proton’s #77 led Saturday’s second session on a 2:19.290, with the Ebimotors #80 and the #88 making it a Porsche 1-2-3, and the best Ferrari, JMW’s, about seven tenths further back. Concern about the Sunday forecast led organisers to bring the race start forward from 12:30 to 10:45.

chapters.title: Cairoli takes pole by seven tenths
text: Cairoli took pole with a 2:15.654, exactly seven tenths clear of Olsen, as Proton Competition locked out the front row with its two Porsches. Pera made it three Porsches on the podium of the session in the Ebimotors car, on 2:17.183, and it was the third consecutive session in which the German manufacturer filled the top three.
The best Ferrari was Molina’s JMW #66, fourth on 2:17.810, narrowly ahead of Griffin in Spirit of Race’s #55 on 2:17.977. Krohn Racing’s #83 was sixth and last on a 2:23.542.

chapters.title: A chaotic, wet run
text: Conditions dominated the class. As the rain strengthened in the second hour the safety car was needed repeatedly, and the GTE order was reshuffled by incidents. Krohn Racing’s #83 was out of the race and was not classified. Proton’s #77 was caught in a collision with LMP2 traffic and dropped far down the order, although the team got it back out before the stoppage.

That left four cars in the fight. When the race was red-flagged, the Ebimotors Porsche was leading with Babini at the wheel, ahead of Spirit of Race’s #55 Ferrari and Proton’s #88. Porsche’s advantage in the conditions had been clear all weekend.

chapters.title: Stopped with the Ebimotors Porsche in front
text: With close to two hours of the four still to run, the race was red-flagged and the cars lined up on the pit straight. Officials later called it off for good. The two-hour mark had been passed, so the result stood and half points were awarded. Ebimotors’ #80 was declared class winner, Spirit of Race’s #55 took second and Proton’s #88 completed the podium.

chapters.title: A first win for Ebimotors
text: The #80 won on 39 laps with Babini, Pera and Curtis credited, the #55 of Cameron, Griffin and Scott second and the Rodas’ and Cairoli’s #88 third, all on the same lap. JMW’s #66 was fourth, one lap down, and Proton’s #77 fifth on 31 laps. Krohn’s #83 was not classified. Pera set the class fastest lap, a 2:41.896.
Proton kept its lead in the table and JMW remained its closest challenger, with the title to be settled at the Portimão finale on 28 October.
